_notes._history: tabs.create:resolve used to be allowlisted here for the native Chrome-vs-Firefox tabs.Tab shape difference (Chrome-only: selected, frozen; Firefox-only: attention, hidden, isArticle, isInReaderMode, sharingState, successorTabId, cookieStoreId). Fixed properly in diff.ts's normalizeTrace instead: any Tab-shaped object (id+windowId+index+boolean active) is now projected down to {url, title, status, index, active} before comparison, so that entire class of divergence is gone.
_notes.tabs.create:resolve: Much smaller residual after the shape-projection fix: verified via re-run that the ONLY remaining difference is the `status` field (chrome: "loading", firefox: "complete") -- both sides otherwise now normalize identically (index, active match; url/title absent on both, matching this extension's permission scope). This is a genuine browser-native timing race in when each engine resolves the tabs.create() promise relative to the new tab's initial paint, not extension or converter behavior, and not fixable by adjusting probe delays (the capture happens synchronously in the shim's promise-then hook, with no artificial wait in between).

extensions.name: OneNote Web Clipper

_notes._offscreen_cascade_root_cause: HISTORICAL (pre-polyfill), root cause #1. OneNote's background script (minified from build/scripts/communicator/offscreenCommunicator.js) calls chrome.runtime.getContexts({contextTypes:[chrome.runtime.ContextType.OFFSCREEN_DOCUMENT], ...}) unconditionally, with no chrome.offscreen feature-detection guard. Before the runtime offscreen polyfill (issue #2), chrome.runtime.ContextType.OFFSCREEN_DOCUMENT was undefined on Firefox and this call threw synchronously ('Expected string instead of undefined'), which silently killed OneNote's entire post-install setup (registerContextMenuItems(), onInstalled(), and invokeClipperInTab()'s actual clip-trigger path all chained off the same unhandled-rejecting clipperIdProcessed promise) -- Firefox produced only 8 traced background events vs Chrome's 36 (measured in this environment at re-triage time; see issue #2 comment for the full before/after numbers). The converter now ships a runtime chrome.offscreen polyfill (chrome.runtime.ContextType.OFFSCREEN_DOCUMENT + a real createDocument/closeDocument backed by a hidden iframe) that unblocks this specific cascade trigger: Firefox now reaches getContexts and createDocument, and the offscreen document itself loads -- but the first message round-trip TO it then fails (see below). See _offscreen_relay_root_cause below for the SECOND, independent root cause the polyfill exposes one layer deeper -- OneNote's clipperIdProcessed chain still never resolves on Firefox, just from a different trigger, so the SAME downstream patterns (getManifest, tabs.create tour, contextMenus.*, etc.) remain chrome-only for a different reason than before.
_notes._offscreen_relay_root_cause: FIXED by shims/runtime-onmessage-compat.js (background.scripts + HTML-page injection via the new html_inject transformer step), chrome2moz issue #8. Was: offscreen.js's chrome.runtime.onMessage listener is declared `async function(e,a,s){...}` and calls sendResponse (`s(...)`) synchronously inside, without ever `return true`-ing; Firefox's native chrome.* compat surface used the async listener's own implicit (undefined) Promise resolution instead of the manually-invoked sendResponse value, so the background's `JSON.parse(e)` on that undefined threw `SyntaxError: JSON.parse: unexpected character`, silently killing the rest of OneNote's post-install setup. Re-measured after the fix (this task, 2026-09-17): Firefox's trace grew from 7 to 26 background events, the JSON.parse error is gone (0 occurrences, was 1), and Firefox now reaches and executes the entire onInstalled() cascade that used to be chrome-only: the getting-started tour tab (tabs.create/onCreated/onUpdated), contextMenus.removeAll, runtime.getManifest, net.fetch (onenote.com/strings) and tabs.query(lastFocusedWindow) all now run identically on both sides (the latter three plus the tabs.create call and contextMenus.create are now byte-identical between browsers -- fully matched, no allowance needed; their entries were removed below). What remains allowed is a smaller, different-in-kind residual: real cross-browser timing/tracing differences on calls BOTH sides now make (tabs.create:resolve, tabs.onCreated:fired, tabs.onUpdated:fired resolve/fire with different url/title/status depending on exactly when each engine's navigation has progressed -- same class as latextocalc's tabs.create:resolve allowance; contextMenus.removeAll and runtime.sendMessage#offscreen fire identically-shaped calls on both sides but the differ can't pair them 1:1, for sendMessage because the payload embeds a fresh random per-run clipperId UUID). See the per-pattern notes below.
_notes._issue_6_reverification: Re-triaged 2026-09-17 after the shim-ordering fix (spy now injects after shims/*.js): Firefox background-event count went from 7 (pre-fix, spy ran before the polyfill so offscreen.*/getContexts were entirely untraced) to 11 (post-fix, spy wraps the polyfill's installed surface so those calls are now traced). The former offscreen.* wildcard allowance is deleted -- offscreen.createDocument, offscreen.createDocument:resolve, and the first runtime.getContexts/runtime.getContexts:resolve pair all now match Chrome byte-for-byte, confirming issue #6 was purely a tracing gap for this entry, not a functional one. This fix landed independently of, and before, the issue #8 relay-crash fix below.
_notes.runtime.getContexts*: Issue #6 tracing gap is fixed (see _issue_6_reverification): the first runtime.getContexts call and its :resolve now match Chrome byte-for-byte on Firefox. Pre-issue-#8-fix, the remaining chrome-only runtime.getContexts/:resolve calls (OneNote's flow calls getContexts again before each subsequent offscreen relay message) were downstream of the relay crash -- Firefox never reached them because it crashed on the first relay round-trip. Issue #8 is now also fixed (see _offscreen_relay_root_cause), so Firefox reaches the later relay messages too; whether those later getContexts/:resolve calls now also match Chrome has not been re-verified against a fresh differential run in this merge (no e2e browser run performed here). Left as a wildcard pending that re-verification -- narrowing to :resolve-only, as already done for the offscreen-gate entry's permanent polyfill-shape divergence, would be premature until re-checked.
_notes.runtime.getURL#<ext>/offscreen.html: Issue #6 tracing blind spot (same as the offscreen-gate corpus entry's note): the polyfill's offscreen.createDocument implementation calls rt.getURL(url) itself to resolve the iframe src, on top of OneNote's own getURL("offscreen.html") call -- this one runs through the untouched, spy-wrapped original, so it shows up as one extra firefox-only call. Pinned to the literal observed args, "<ext>/offscreen.html" -- unlike the offscreen-gate entry's plain "offscreen.html", OneNote's own code resolves the URL to an absolute extension URL BEFORE passing it into createDocument's {url} option, so when the polyfill's rt.getURL(url) call receives that already-absolute URL, the trace normalizer rewrites it to the <ext>/... form. Verified against the actual trace file, not assumed.
_notes.runtime.sendMessage#offscreen: Post-fix re-triage (issue #8 fixed): both sides now send the remove-from-local-storage/set-to-local-storage (clipperId) messages, byte-identical in shape -- but each carries a freshly generated random clipperId UUID ("ON-<uuid>"), regenerated every run, so Chrome's and Firefox's copies never share a literal value and the differ reports one chrome-only and one firefox-only event per message instead of a match. This is a harness/differ limitation (no content-independent matching for random-nonce payloads), not a functional divergence: the round-trip itself now succeeds identically on both sides. Pinned to the substring "offscreen" via api#substring so other runtime.sendMessage call sites (contentCaptureInject.js, logManager.js, regionOverlay.js -- the actual clip flow, not currently probed) are NOT masked if probes are later extended to exercise them.
_notes.tabs.create:resolve: Post-fix re-triage (issue #8 fixed): Firefox now calls tabs.create for the getting-started tour tab too (previously chrome-only, zero Firefox events). The call itself (tabs.create#getting-started, url pinned) is now byte-identical on both sides and needs no allowance. Only :resolve still diverges, and only in the same way latextocalc's does: Chrome resolves the promise before navigation starts (url/title empty, status "loading"); Firefox resolves after navigation to about:blank has begun (title already showing the target page's slug, status "complete"). A genuine browser-native timing race, not extension or converter behavior -- same class as the latextocalc allowance, now also present here because Firefox finally reaches this code path.
_notes.tabs.onCreated:fired: Same timing race as tabs.create:resolve above, now observed on both sides post-fix (previously chrome-only only). Left name-only (not pinned): Chrome's snapshot is {url:"",title:"",status:"loading",...} at fire time; Firefox's already shows the resolved title/status -- no single substring covers both shapes.
_notes.tabs.onUpdated:fired: Same tour-tab navigation, now firing on both sides post-fix with different per-step ordering/content (favIconUrl format, isArticle timing) as each engine's navigation progresses at its own pace. Widened from the old "getting-started"-pinned substring to name-only since Firefox's early onUpdated events (before the URL is set) no longer contain that substring but are still part of the same real, expected cross-browser sequence -- an onUpdated divergence for an unrelated URL would still surface distinctly since this extension only ever navigates the one tour tab in these probes.
_notes.pingProbe (harness fix, not an allowed_d: probes.ts's pingProbe checks contentScriptsCoverUrl(manifest, fixtureUrl) BEFORE opening any pages (same check contentProbe already used), skipping immediately when content_scripts can't cover the fixture origin -- which is OneNote's case (content_scripts only match onenote.officeapps.live.com). This keeps the harness's own probe-driven fixture-tab opens from producing a second, unrelated source of tabs.onCreated:fired/tabs.onUpdated:fired divergence tangled up with the tour-tab one documented above.
_notes.contextMenus.removeAll: Post-fix re-triage (issue #8 fixed): contextMenus.create (one per clip action) is now byte-identical on both sides and needs no allowance. contextMenus.removeAll still shows as one chrome-only + one firefox-only event despite identical args (["[fn]"]) on both sides -- a differ pairing artifact (surrounding event order/interleaving differs enough between the two traces that the matcher can't align this single call), not a functional divergence. Narrowed from the old contextMenus.* wildcard now that .create is matched.
_notes.management.uninstallSelf*: Kept from the original task spec as a defensive/regression-guard pattern. Investigated: this pinned version (3.11.2) does not declare the `management` permission at all and never calls management.uninstallSelf in either trace, so the pattern is currently inert (matches nothing). Left in place in case a future re-pin reintroduces browser-detection + self-uninstall behavior, per the binding decision that this entry exists partly to catch that regression.

extensions._note: gates nothing until a fixture host matching its content_scripts (onenote.officeapps.live.com) exists -- tracked in issue #5

_notes.runtime.getContexts:resolve: Issue #6 fix verified (re-triaged 2026-09-17): the spy shim now runs AFTER shims/offscreen-polyfill.js, so it wraps the polyfill's already-installed chrome.runtime.getContexts override instead of a pre-polyfill stub. The plain runtime.getContexts call and its args now match byte-for-byte on both sides (no longer in allowed_diffs -- deleted, along with the former offscreen.* wildcard, since every offscreen.createDocument/:resolve, offscreen.hasDocument, and offscreen.closeDocument call now matches identically too). Only :resolve's content still genuinely diverges: Chrome's native getContexts resolves with a documentId-keyed context object (real browser internals, e.g. {"contextId":"f19bfdfe-...","documentId":"81F0D712...",...}); the polyfill's emulated resolve uses a documentUrl-keyed shape with a synthetic contextId ("c2m-offscreen-0") and no documentId field at all. This is a genuine, permanent shape difference between the polyfill's emulation and native browser internals, not a tracing gap -- not pinned to a substring because Chrome's contextId/documentId are random per-run UUIDs, so no stable substring exists on that side.
_notes.runtime.getURL#offscreen.html: The polyfill's offscreen.createDocument implementation calls rt.getURL(url) itself (to resolve the iframe src), in addition to the extension's own t.getURL("offscreen.html") call -- so Firefox observes one extra runtime.getURL call the spy shim did capture (this one runs through the untouched original, unlike getContexts above). Pinned to the literal URL since this extension has only one; a runtime.getURL divergence for any other URL is NOT masked.
_notes._issue_8_regression_control: Was a deliberate, decisive control for chrome2moz issue #8: an `async` onMessage listener that calls sendResponse synchronously without `return true`, the exact shape of OneNote Web Clipper's offscreen-relay listener. Fixed by shims/runtime-onmessage-compat.js (background.scripts + HTML-page injection via the new html_inject transformer step): the shim suppresses the async listener's own Promise when sendResponse already answered synchronously, so Firefox now delivers the real sendResponse value (Chrome's precedence) instead of resolving to undefined. Verified: the gate now passes with NO issue-#8 allowance -- runtime.sendMessage:resolve and storage.local.set both carry the real "hello async offscreen" text on Firefox, matching Chrome. The four allowances that used to gate this divergence (runtime.sendMessage:resolve#null, runtime.sendMessage:resolve#hello async offscreen, storage.local.set#UNDEFINED_RESPONSE, storage.local.set#hello async offscreen) have been removed; their reappearance would mean the fix regressed.

_notes._purpose: Kill/wake probe gate (spec Probes #5). Background counts boots in storage.local; killWakeProbe boots it, kills the background (Chromium CDP ServiceWorker.stopAllWorkers; Firefox idle timeout), then opens a second fixture tab to wake it via tabs.onUpdated. The content script reads storage.local on each page so the boot counter reaches the trace. Both sides killed+rebooted => boots go 1 -> 2 identically and MATCH.
_notes.tabs.onUpdated:fired: The gate registers a top-level tabs.onUpdated listener as its wake trigger, and the spy traces every firing. Chrome and Firefox emit genuinely different native tab-lifecycle sequences for the same probe-driven navigations (Chrome: about:blank loading/complete then the fixture; Firefox: New Tab titles, an isArticle change, different ordering and tab indexes), observed as 39 tabs.onUpdated:fired-only divergences in CI once the random bootMark was removed. This is engine noise, not kill/wake behavior, and it is NOT the gate's evidence: the assertion is the storage.local boot counter (storage.local.set {boots, lastWake} in the background and storage.local.get:resolve in the content script), which is content-pinned, MATCHED on both sides in that same run, and would still diverge if a side failed to reboot after the kill. Same class as LatexToCalc's tabs.create:resolve and OneNote's tabs.onUpdated:fired#getting-started allowances.
_notes._firefox_kill_confirmed: The kill/wake spike (spikes/RESULTS.md, Kill/Wake section) confirmed, three runs in a row, that Firefox's converted event-page background does idle-terminate past extensions.background.idle.timeout under headless Selenium/WebDriver and reboots (fresh top-level execution, observed via a bootMark that can only change on a genuine restart) on the next tabs.onUpdated-triggering event. No kill-unsupported allowance is needed; both sides are expected to reboot and match.

_notes._purpose: Exercises the clipboard readback observable (issue #4.3): a content script writes a fixed string and reads it back. The spy shim records clipboard.writeText and clipboard.readText:resolve on both browsers; with clipboard permissions pre-granted by the drivers, both resolve identically, so the content-context traces MATCH with no allowance. A regression that changed the clipboard value (or dropped the read-back) would diverge and fail here.
